items.title: Engine-cover insulation chafing fuel return hose and wiring
items.summary: Insulation in the engine cover can wear through the fuel return hose and a wiring harness; dealers fitted steel lines and rerouted the wiring.

items.title: Fuel-pump oil pressure switch missing seal
items.summary: A missing seal lets contaminants into the switch that powers the fuel pump, so it can fail open or closed.

items.title: Cruise control cable can freeze
items.summary: Water in the cable can freeze and stop the cruise control releasing; dealers replaced and rerouted the actuator and cable.

items.title: Fuel tank can expand into the propshaft
items.summary: In heat above 95°F the tank can swell against its shield and be holed by the propeller shaft; dealers added a supplemental vent system.

items.title: Accelerator pedal shaft corrosion
items.summary: The pedal shaft's coating reacts with its bronze bushing and can corrode, raising friction; dealers fitted a revised pedal and shaft.

items.title: Master cylinder fastened with metric nuts
items.summary: The master cylinder was attached to the Hydroboost with metric nuts instead of the required inch-thread nuts.

items.title: Brake lines chafing between master cylinder and ABS modulator
items.summary: The flexible lines can chafe and leak; dealers replaced them.

items.title: Turn signals fail to cancel
items.summary: The plastic cancelling pin in the switch can wear; dealers fitted a switch with a metal pin.

items.title: Wrong steering-gear mounting hardware
items.summary: Some Alphas were assembled with an incorrect combination of steering-gear-to-frame hardware; dealers inspected and corrected it.

tsbs.title: Transfer case cooler loop leak ('the vampire')
tsbs.ref: AM General Customer Satisfaction Campaign R0101 (September 2001)
tsbs.summary: Cracks at the cooler loop's welded fittings let transmission fluid flow into the transfer case, draining the transmission. The revised loop has a bracing angle and tab, and a light-blue band on one hose connection.

timeline.change: Civilian Hummer launches: mechanical 6.2 diesel (150 hp), 3L80 three-speed, 25-gal tank, batteries under the passenger seat, non-adjustable seats. Sold factory-direct at first. 316 built
Electronic 6.5 diesel (170 hp, 290 lb-ft) and 4L80-E four-speed; batteries move under the hood; new HVAC, adjustable seats, catalytic converter
5.7 gas V8 option (23-gal tank, 24-in fording); extended-cab pickup and full-door open top added; wagon gets barn doors. From VIN 163985, stronger steering arms, center link and ball joints

6.5 turbo diesel arrives (190 hp, 385 lb-ft) with a second fuel tank on every truck; new CTIS with solenoid valves; body raised 3/4 in; gas engine dropped mid-year. Start of the No. 8-cylinder crack risk period
Turbo diesel to 195 hp and 430 lb-ft with oil-cooled pistons; sound insulation; Detroit Locker optional. From VIN 176477 ('97.5') a much better redesigned HVAC system
Axle ratio changes from 2.73 to 2.56; eccentric camber adjustment; quieter geared hubs. The last year of Torsen I and no ABS; Flash Off-Road calls it the quintessential pre-Alpha H1
ABS, TorqTrac4 traction control and Torsen II differentials; naturally aspirated diesel dropped. AM General starts fitting improved 6.5 blocks from May. GM buys the Hummer brand in December
Slant-back body offered (39 built, per Flash Off-Road); 16.5-in and 17-in aluminum wheel options; redesigned cabin. Later 2000 trucks (after VIN 137ZA9037YE188469) not at risk of the No. 8 crack
First AM General-built 6.5 engines ('F' in the fourth VIN digit); redesigned gauges and heated mirrors
Higher torque-bias differentials; H1 badging; 10th Anniversary edition of 65 orange wagons; two- and four-door hardtops dropped except for fleets
Optional Eaton electric rear locker; factory leather and heated seats
'Optimizer' 6.5 turbo diesel with Caterpillar-built ECM (205 hp, 440 lb-ft); all-new interior; optional front and rear Eaton lockers. No 2005 model year follows
H1 Alpha: 6.6 Duramax (300 hp, 520 lb-ft), Allison five-speed, 2-in body lift, helical-gear hubs, 12-in brakes, 51 gal of fuel. 729 built; production ends June 2006

identify.intro: H1s were updated mid-year, re-engined by owners and sometimes built from military parts, so the VIN and the hardware tell you more than the title's model year.

items.head: VIN engine and transmission codes
items.body: Fourth digit is the engine: X = 6.2 diesel, Y = 6.5 non-turbo diesel, Z = GM 6.5 turbo diesel, F = 6.5 turbo diesel with Caterpillar ECM, D/L = 5.7 L05 gas, W = 350 gas. Fifth digit: E = 3L80 three-speed, A = 4L80-E four-speed. On the 2006 Alpha the fourth digit is P (Duramax) and the fifth H (Allison).

items.head: VIN body and year codes
items.body: Digits 6–7 give the body: 82 VLC2 two-door truck, 83 HMC4 four-door truck, 84 HMCS wagon, 85 VLCO open top, 86 HMCF fleet, 87/88 Recruit, 89 XLC2 extended cab, 90 HMCO open top with full hard doors. Digit 10 is the model year (N = 1992 … 4 = 2004, 6 = 2006) and digit 11 is the plant (E = Mishawaka).

items.head: Spotting an Alpha
items.body: A square intake cap in place of the round 'mushroom', a Duramax badge on the hood, a hood hinged at the bottom center, a brush guard without its top bar, and a black block-off strip above the rear bumper filling the 2-in body-lift gap. Wave 2 trucks (from September 2005, first VIN 6E226861) have an all-black interior.

items.head: Torsen type and axle ratio
items.body: Differential covers normally carry a tag with the ratio and Torsen type. Otherwise read the ring-gear tooth count: 41/15 is 2.73:1, 41/16 is 2.56:1. All trucks through 1998 have Torsen I; 1998 is the only Torsen I truck with 2.56 gears.

items.head: Old or upgraded HVAC
items.body: Pre-'97.5 control heads have extra recirculate and A/C buttons and an electric heater valve. The upgraded system uses a vacuum-controlled heater valve, with small colored vacuum tubes behind the control head.

items.head: 6.5 block casting
items.body: The definitive check for the improved No. 8-cylinder block is the casting number, readable only with the engine cover off: C-159 (March 15, 1999) and later are the revised design.

values.intro: H1 prices are well off the new-truck sticker but strong for clean, documented trucks. The Alpha and Duramax conversions sit in a different bracket.
values.note: Based on about 50 Bring a Trailer H1 sales from January 2025 to October 2026. Drivers sold for $30,500–60,255. Low-mileage trucks and a 2002 10th Anniversary reached $62,000–101,500. Stock Alphas sold for $120,000–146,000, and Duramax conversions for $73,000–212,500.
